items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master’s degree in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, psychology, social sciences, or a related field.
Doctoral degree in public health, epidemiology, psychology, health services research, or a related field.
Minimum of 4-7 years of experience in research data analysis.
Experience preparing IRB applications, amendments, and continuing reviews.
Experience conducting statistical analyses of health, survey, or program data using statistical software.
Experience working with electronic health record data or standardized clinical and mental health assessment data.
Experience managing, cleaning, and documenting large or complex datasets.
Experience analyzing longitudinal data and applying multivariate methods.
Experience handling confidential or protected data in compliance with privacy regulations such as HIPAA and FERPA.
Experience contributing to peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations.
Experience supporting human subjects research.
Experience higher education student health, counseling, or well-being settings.
Experience preparing reports, tables, and data visualizations that communicate findings to non-technical audiences.

Statistical analysis. Conducts statistical analyses of clinical, survey, and program data, including longitudinal and multi-year datasets, using appropriate descriptive, inferential, and multivariate methods. Recommends statistical approaches and identifies trends, interrelationships, and data uses. Interprets results and summarizes findings for the PI and HWS units, with a focus on mental and medical health outcomes. (25% time)

Study design and IRB. Under the direction of the PI, contributes to the planning and design of research and evaluation studies, including protocol development, sampling procedures, and the design and testing of data collection instruments. Prepares, submits, and maintains IRB applications, amendments, and continuing reviews. (15% time)

Data management and compliance. Manages, cleans, links, and documents research data drawn from electronic health records, standardized clinical assessment instruments, and program records. Defines the logical structure of datasets, audits data for accuracy and completeness, and maintains secure data storage and access procedures. Ensures all data handling complies with HIPAA, FERPA, approved IRB protocols, and University data security policies. Participates in developing and implementing data security procedures. (15% time)

Dashboards and reporting systems. Develops systems for organizing data to analyze, identify, and report trends. Designs and maintains data dashboards and visualizations that communicate service utilization, program outcomes, and student health and well-being trends to HWS leadership and campus stakeholders. Prepares data for presentation and assists in transmitting findings to users. (15% time)

Data collection. Coordinates data collection activities across HWS units, including survey administration, data extraction requests, and tracking of response and retention across study time points. Monitors data collection procedures for fidelity and quality. (10% time)

Publications and presentations. Contributes to peer-reviewed manuscripts, technical reports, and presentations of research findings. Prepares tables, figures, methods sections, and results summaries. Prepares reports of studies for internal validation and program evaluation. (10% time)

Consultation and collaboration. Collaborates with clinical and program staff in Student Health Services, Counseling & Psychological Services, Case Management, SWIFT, and The Well to identify data needs and research questions. Provides research and data support for cross-departmental HWS projects as required. Maintains professional expertise in research methods and health data analysis. (5% time)
Other duties as assigned. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Frequently
Communicate Orally: Frequently
Reason & Analyze: Frequently
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Constantly
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally
Thorough knowledge of the research function, including study design, sampling, instrument development, and data collection methods.
Knowledge of IRB policies and procedures and the human subjects research review process.
Thorough skills in statistical analysis and data programming, including descriptive, inferential, and multivariate methods.
Knowledge of electronic health record data structures and standardized mental and medical health assessment instruments.
Research skills at a level to evaluate alternate solutions and develop recommendations.
Knowledge of research methods and literature related to college student health, mental health, and well-being.
Working knowledge of HIPAA, FERPA, and human subjects protections, and the ability to handle confidential information with discretion.
Ability to work collaboratively with clinical, program, and administrative staff across multiple units.
Skills in scientific writing for peer-reviewed publication.
